title: Paul Whiteman, Henry Busse and bandsmen buying records
summary: He recalls Whiteman's records and a Berlin dealer's pride in Henry Busse; the band bought records like hot cakes, with Bix, Trumbauer and Miff Mole as influences.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: That was before Paul Whiteman. That was entirely different. Then at about the same time, Paul Whiteman -- I heard Paul Whiteman's record, with Bussey the trumpet player.
Henry Bussey, playin 'Runnin' Wild,' I think that's the name of it.
And they -- the proprietor of the music store was very proud and happy
because he said, 'Bussef, we know he was from Berliner.' He was from Berlin.
He was originally. And they were very happy, and so, we -- in our profession, what comes from the other side and what we try to do, all helps to further the path.
That we are trying to continue.
Well, I'm trying to get onto the effect of these American Jazz records that began to come over there.
Was there a lot of influence on the players here, were they all sort of excited by these records?
Most of the boys in the band, naturally, they're all excited.
They bought the recordings like hot cakes.
And most of them, if they didn't imitate them exactly, they used -- there was a certain influence on their playing.
You see. As a guide to them.
We used -- yes, their recordings were simply terrific, and that other guy, this famous saxophone player, Frank Trumbauer, --
Yes, he was simply terrific with Bix.
So Bix and Trumbauer and Nichols, these were big influences.
